scenes.visual: Title card '107 Bottles' over a rack of small fly bottles. Same colour map as the first film: COLOUR MAP, same in both films: GOLD bead/bar = one allele (the 'gold' allele); BLUE bead = the other allele; a WHITE TRIANGLE under the axis = the mean (average) allele frequency across replicates; a horizontal axis labelled 'frequency of gold' runs 0 to 1. Cream background, 16:9. Every number appears only as on-screen text. Beads and bags are simple cartoons; dot clouds and histograms are computed from a Wright-Fisher model and labelled 'computed'; anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'. Histogram bars are GOLD.

scenes.tts: To see drift's scatter, you need many populations at once. Do real animals spread apart like the beads, with their average left alone?
scenes.visual: A brief recap: the first film's dot cloud widening over the 0-to-1 axis while the WHITE TRIANGLE wobbles slightly around 0.5. The beads dissolve into small fruit-fly cartoons.
scenes.narration: To see drift's scatter, you need many populations at once. Do real animals spread apart like the beads, with their average left alone?

scenes.tts: From one bottle's frequency alone, you could not tell. Follow one line alone. It climbs, dips and climbs again. Was it pushed, or was it luck?
scenes.visual: One fly bottle. Beside it a single line graph, generation 0 to 19 on the x axis, frequency of gold 0 to 1 on the y axis, traces a jagged random walk from 0.5 (computed, one Wright-Fisher run). A question mark sits at its end.
scenes.narration: From one bottle's frequency alone, you could not tell. Follow one line alone. It climbs, dips and climbs again. Was it pushed, or was it luck?

scenes.tts: Peter Buri published the real experiment, with fruit flies. He followed two alleles of a gene for eye colour, the brown locus.
scenes.visual: Name card 'Peter Buri, Evolution, 1956'. A cartoon fruit fly with a highlighted eye; label 'two alleles at the brown eye-colour locus', one coloured GOLD and one BLUE.
scenes.narration: Peter Buri published the real experiment, with fruit flies. He followed two alleles of a gene for eye colour, the brown locus.

scenes.tts: Every line started at one half gold. Each generation, he picked sixteen flies as the parents of the next. His first series had a hundred and seven lines.
scenes.visual: A rack of bottles fills row by row; counter '107 lines'. Inside one bottle, 16 fly icons light up, labelled '16 parents each generation'. On-screen: 'start: 0.5', '19 generations'.
scenes.narration: Every line started at one half gold. Each generation, he picked sixteen flies as the parents of the next. His first series had a hundred and seven lines.

scenes.tts: Every bottle was set up the same way and kept the same way. So chance alone predicts differences between the lines.
scenes.visual: The 107 bottles shown identical, a check mark over the rack labelled 'replicates: same start, same conditions'.
scenes.narration: Every bottle was set up the same way and kept the same way. So chance alone predicts differences between the lines.

scenes.tts: Now stack all the lines into one picture. Each bar counts how many lines sit at each frequency. At the start, every line is in the middle bar.
scenes.visual: The bottles drop down into a histogram over the 0-to-1 axis: bins of width 1/16, plus separate bars at exactly 0 and exactly 1. At generation 0 one tall GOLD bar at 0.5 holds all 107 lines. WHITE TRIANGLE under 0.5. Label, kept on screen through s14: 'bars: illustration built with Buri's estimate, Ne = 9.0; not his data'.
scenes.narration: Now stack all the lines into one picture. Each bar counts how many lines sit at each frequency. At the start, every line is in the middle bar.

scenes.tts: Generation by generation, the pile flattens. Lines drift up and down. Some lose blue entirely, some lose gold, and those stay at the edges.
scenes.visual: Generation counter ticks 0 to 10. The central bar sinks and spreads into a flat plateau; bars at exactly 0 and exactly 1 begin to grow (lines that lost one allele), drawn in darker outline as 'fixed or lost'.
scenes.narration: Generation by generation, the pile flattens. Lines drift up and down. Some lose blue entirely, some lose gold, and those stay at the edges.

scenes.tts: By generation ten, the edges are filling up. Now watch the white triangle, the pooled frequency across all lines. By generation nineteen, will it be up, down, or still at one half?
scenes.visual: Counter frozen at 10. The WHITE TRIANGLE pulses under the axis. Three option tags float above it: 'up', 'down', 'still 0.5'.
scenes.narration: By generation ten, the edges are filling up. Now watch the white triangle, the pooled frequency across all lines. By generation nineteen, will it be up, down, or still at one half?

scenes.visual: Hold the frame; a 5-second countdown; caption 'Predict: where is the triangle at generation 19?'.

scenes.tts: Still at about one half. By then many lines had ended with only one allele. Yet the pooled frequency showed no systematic change.
scenes.visual: Counter runs 10 to 19. The histogram becomes U-shaped: tall bars at 0 and 1, a low flat middle. The WHITE TRIANGLE wobbles slightly around 0.5 with no sustained trend; the tag 'about 0.5: no systematic change' lights up.
scenes.narration: Still at about one half. By then many lines had ended with only one allele. Yet the pooled frequency showed no systematic change.

scenes.tts: Spread without a push on the average. That is the pattern drift predicts, now seen in real flies rather than beads.
scenes.visual: Two labels snap on: a bracket over the U 'spread: grew', an arrow at the triangle 'average: no systematic change'. Banner 'the drift prediction'.
scenes.narration: Spread without a push on the average. That is the pattern drift predicts, now seen in real flies rather than beads.

scenes.tts: But how fast did the lines spread? Buri asked how big an ideal population would have to be to spread that fast.
scenes.visual: Freeze the histogram at generation 19. A stopwatch icon. Card 'how big an ideal population would spread this fast?'
scenes.narration: But how fast did the lines spread? Buri asked how big an ideal population would have to be to spread that fast.

scenes.tts: Here is the spread computed for an ideal population of sixteen. Buri's real lines spread faster than that, with more of them at the edges.
scenes.visual: A translucent outline histogram, 'computed: ideal population of 16', overlays the GOLD illustration bars at generation 19: its edge bars are clearly shorter and its middle taller. Label 'ideal 16: slower than Buri's lines'.
scenes.narration: Here is the spread computed for an ideal population of sixteen. Buri's real lines spread faster than that, with more of them at the edges.

scenes.tts: From how fast his own lines spread, Buri estimated about nine. They drifted as if each bottle held only nine flies.
scenes.visual: The 16 outline fades. On-screen card 'Buri's mean estimate from his data, first series: Ne = 9.0' beside '16 flies in each bottle'. The GOLD bars keep their label 'illustration built with Ne = 9.0; not a fit'.
scenes.narration: From how fast his own lines spread, Buri estimated about nine. They drifted as if each bottle held only nine flies.

scenes.tts: That number is the effective population size. Faster spread means a smaller effective size. It measures how hard chance acted, not how many flies were in the bottle.
scenes.caption: That number is the effective population size, Ne. Faster spread means a smaller effective size. It measures how hard chance acted, not how many flies were in the bottle.
scenes.visual: Bottle with 16 fly icons; 9 of them glow as a label 'effective size: how hard chance acted' and the bottle label reads 'census: 16'. The glow is labelled 'schematic: not 9 particular flies'.
scenes.narration: That number is the effective population size, Ne. Faster spread means a smaller effective size. It measures how hard chance acted, not how many flies were in the bottle.

scenes.tts: So one line wanders, and tells you little about cause. Many replicates, side by side, show whether the average was pushed.
scenes.visual: The single jagged line from the opening reappears small at left; at right the full U-shaped histogram with its WHITE TRIANGLE near 0.5. An arrow from the line to the histogram labelled 'replicates reveal the average'.
scenes.narration: So one line wanders, and tells you little about cause. Many replicates, side by side, show whether the average was pushed.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Take-home line: 'One line wanders; replicates show whether the average was pushed.'
